theme: UPGo (McGill) and strr R package: STR research tooling and datasets for Canada/US cities
queries_run: gh search repos "strr short term rental r package"
gh api users/UPGo-McGill ; gh search repos org:UPGo-McGill
gh search repos "short-term rental" r language:R --sort updated
WebFetch on strr README, cmhcr README, str-regulation-housing, Local-law-18-vs-Short-term-rentals

candidates.name: strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (McGill Urban Politics and Governance lab). Functions to process raw AirDNA 'property' and 'daily' files: table compression/expansion, listing location estimation, commercial-operator identification, frequently-rented entire-home-listing detection, 'ghost hostel' clustering, housing-unit classification. No sample/committed data (works on externally-supplied licensed AirDNA extracts); MIT-style repo, no CRAN release, 5 stars, last updated 25 Aug 2025 (master branch).
candidates.why_useful: Directly named in the theme; is the canonical open-source method for turning raw AirDNA property/daily files into realised-occupancy/ADR-style STR metrics -- exactly gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs). We would still need our own AirDNA-equivalent extract to run it, but the cleaning/classification logic (ghost hostels, commercial-operator flags) is reusable on any STR daily-calendar data including our own Inside Airbnb captures.
candidates.last_activity: 2025-08-25 (per API updatedAt; package targets ongoing dev)
candidates.geography: Canada/US STR markets generically (package is data-source-agnostic)
candidates.size_hint: small R package (R/, tests/, docs/ only)

candidates.name: upgo
candidates.what_it_holds: UPGo lab's general utility R package (companion to strr) for their STR/housing research pipeline. No committed datasets found in the root listing.
candidates.why_useful: Supporting tooling for the same AirDNA/STR pipeline as strr; low standalone value but worth noting alongside strr since some strr functions may depend on it.

candidates.name: cmhcr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package to 'Import and Clean CMHC Data Tables' -- CMHC (Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation) is Canada's federal housing agency publishing rental market survey vacancy rates, average rents, starts/completions by CMA. Package is an import/clean client, not a bundled dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Fills the Canada leg of gap #13 (long-term rental/housing economics, host supply side) with a ready-made client for CMHC's official rental market data, useful for STR<->LTR crossover analysis in Canadian markets (Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal) where UPGo/strr's other repos already do STR-side work.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever CMHC's public tables cover (multi-year, updated annually by CMHC)
candidates.size_hint: small package, no bundled CSVs found

candidates.name: canada-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis code (R/ folder only, no data dir) for Combs et al. 2019 'Short-Term Rentals in Canada: Uneven Growth, Uneven Impacts' -- national Airbnb-activity study. Underlying AirDNA data not committed (licensed, gitignored).
candidates.why_useful: Points to a published academic study quantifying Canadian Airbnb growth/impact by city; methodology repo only, but confirms the study exists and how UPGo processes national STR panels -- relevant if the memo wants a Canada-wide STR growth benchmark.
candidates.last_activity: 2019 (per repo age; API updatedAt 2025-08-25 reflects a metadata touch)

candidates.name: toronto-report
candidates.what_it_holds: Bookdown report source ('Analysis of Toronto's STR registration system') with chapters on market overview, housing impacts, COVID-era returning listings, regulatory compliance. Has a data/ folder but it is empty (only .DS_Store) -- raw STR data is gitignored/licensed, not committed.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Toronto STR registration-compliance analysis exists (regulation angle, gap #12) but no usable data is actually in the repo -- catalogue as method-only pointer.
candidates.size_hint: report source only, no data files

candidates.name: str-ltr-mtl-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Code for a report on short-term rentals 'returning to the long-term market' in Montreal -- the STR-to-LTR conversion question directly. R/ and output/ and photos/ dirs; no committed raw dataset (licensed AirDNA input assumed, gitignored).
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-point for gap #13's STR<->LTR crossover question, with a concrete Montreal case study methodology, even though no data ships with the repo.

candidates.name: mtl_landlords
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper code to collect Montreal landlord/ownership data (property registry style) -- housing supply-side, not Airbnb-specific.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: landlord-concentration data could feed a housing-supply angle for STR<->LTR crossover, but it targets a non-Airbnb municipal/registry site and is scraper-only (no committed data).

candidates.name: bc-report-2024
candidates.what_it_holds: R/ and output/ dirs for a 2024 British Columbia STR report (BC introduced a province-wide STR registration law in 2024). No data/ folder visible; data presumably licensed AirDNA input, gitignored.
candidates.why_useful: Recency is notable (2024 report on BC's new province-wide STR law) -- relevant to gap #12 (STR ordinance tracker) as a pointer to a fresh regulatory-impact study, though no data is committed.

candidates.name: montreal-finance-2022
candidates.what_it_holds: Code for 'High rises and housing stress: A spatial big-data analysis of rental housing financialization' -- Montreal rental-housing financialization study (highest-starred UPGo repo, 6 stars). No committed raw dataset found at root.
candidates.why_useful: Housing-financialization angle on host supply economics; tangential to gap #13 but a genuine published methodology, not just an Airbnb rehash.

candidates.name: str-regulation-housing
candidates.what_it_holds: ETH Zurich master's thesis (2024) replication package, 'Regulatory Repercussions: how municipal short-term rental regulation affects US housing costs'. Two committed CSVs: regulatory_data.csv (131 US cities across 44 states, coded municipal STR-ordinance 'prohibitiveness scores' 0.5-5.0 covering hosted vs. unhosted rental rules and enforcement mechanisms) and longitudinal_data.csv (2,431 city-month panel rows, 24 California cities, 2015-2023, combining prohibitiveness scores with rental costs, property values, and demographic/economic covariates). Codebooks included; raw ordinance PDFs and MAXQDA project not included but coded results are. MIT licensed.
candidates.why_useful: Strong direct hit on gap #12 (STR ordinance tracker / city registration datasets, US-wide with a quantified prohibitiveness score across 131 cities/44 states) and gap #13 (STR-housing-cost crossover panel, CA cities 2015-2023) -- a genuinely new, committed, structured dataset outside anything we currently hold.
candidates.geography: United States (131 cities/44 states regulatory panel; 24 California cities longitudinal panel)
candidates.time_coverage: 2015-2023 (longitudinal panel); regulatory panel is current as coded (2024 thesis)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: not a duplicate; new to our regulatory event database (32 factors) -- longer time span and quantified score, worth cross-checking against our existing 32-factor database for overlap/extension

notes: Searched via gh search repos + gh api contents listings (5 search calls total, within the 6-call budget; one call hit a 403 rate limit and was retried successfully after a 40s sleep per instructions). UPGo-McGill is a real, active McGill research org (58 public repos) built around the strr package, but essentially all their city-analysis repos (canada, toronto, montreal, whitehorse, bc-report-2024) follow the same pattern: R/ analysis code + report Rmds + an empty or gitignored data/ folder, because their underlying input is licensed AirDNA data they cannot redistribute. So the org's real value to us is the strr package itself (a genuine open-source AirDNA-processing method addressing gap #2) plus cmhcr (Canada housing data client, gap #13) -- not raw datasets. The standout unexpected find was jastephan63/str-regulation-housing, a 2024 ETH Zurich thesis replication package with two committed, structured CSVs (US ordinance prohibitiveness scores + CA rental-cost panel) that is a genuine new dataset for gaps #12/#13 and was found via the broader 'short-term rental R language:R' query rather than the UPGo-specific terms. kterdal/Local-law-18-vs-Short-term-rentals looked promising given our NYC LL18 gap but turned out to be a poster-only repo (R script + PDF, no committed data) and was excluded. Did not use gh search code. Did not clone or run anything.
